ambiguities: Odette is the explicit object of the anonymous letter's accusations and of Swann's climactic question, but her local standing here remains deliberately unresolved ('il comprit que c'était peut-être vrai') and is inseparable from the already-captured diminishment of Swann's own reasoning; she was left unscored rather than assigned a speculative direction.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Prends garde, je saurai bien te dégeler, tu n'es pas de marbre » ; Odette's remembered account, « Mme Verdurin, en ce moment il n'y en a que pour moi... elle m'embrasse... elle veut que je la tutoie » ; culminating in Swann's direct question to Odette, « Dis-moi si c'était vrai, avec elle ou avec une autre. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann retroactively reinterprets a joking remark and Odette's account of Mme Verdurin's affection as evidence of a possible improper intimacy, casting fresh suspicion on Mme Verdurin and driving the passage's closing confrontation.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Swann n'avait jamais rencontré personne qui... vînt à lui avec une parole plus sentie, un geste plus discret et plus juste » set against « cette vie peu honorable qu'il menait » and the concluding verdict, « Orsan n'en a peut-être pas [de coeur], mais ce n'est pas un honnête homme. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann praises d'Orsan as the most delicately sympathetic of his friends, but his known compromised reputation leads Swann to a starkly negative final verdict that sets him apart from the more favorably judged Charlus and prince des Laumes.

status_effects.explanation: A retroactively reinterpreted memory casts uncertain but real suspicion of improper closeness with Odette onto Mme Verdurin, mildly lowering her local standing in Swann's eyes.

Despite being praised as unusually delicate and sympathetic, d'Orsan is ultimately judged by Swann to be 'not an honest man' because of his known dishonorable conduct, a distinctly negative verdict compared to the friends judged around him.
